title: HarnessAI project contract (harness.toml)
description: The single contract of a HarnessAI project. Keys marked `preset` get their default from the chosen preset (catalog/presets/); `asked` keys are settled during the interview; `derived` keys are computed or filled by the AI; `open` tables accept any key. Custom keywords: x-source, x-values (meaning of each enum value), x-effect (what the key changes in the project).

schema_version.description: Version of the contract format. Bumped only on breaking changes to this schema.

description.description: One-sentence pitch: what it does and for whom.

preset.description: Quality preset providing the defaults of every `preset` key.

x-values.prototype: show an idea or a UX to someone; may be thrown away
x-values.poc: prove a technical feasibility (one risky question); thrown away
x-values.mvp: first usable version for real users
x-values.small: a project meant to last, limited scope
x-values.large: production, many features, long-lived, possibly a team

types.description: Free tags describing the kind of project (e.g. web, mobile, backend, iot, cli, data). Guides the AI when deriving domain stack dimensions and standards.

license.description: SPDX licence identifier (e.g. MIT, Apache-2.0), or `none`.

languages.description: Languages used in the project. Codes such as `en`, `fr`, `pt-BR`.
languages.x-effect: `docs`: framing docs and AGENTS.md prose; `code`: identifiers and comments; `commits`: proposed commit messages. The interview proposes the user's language for `docs`.

stack.description: Pillars of the technical stack, as `<dimension> = "<choice>"` (e.g. `frontend = "react"`). Dimensions are free: universal ones come from catalog/stack/, domain ones are derived by the AI. The justified detail (versions, rationale, alternatives, phase) lives in docs/STACK.md.

imposed.description: Dimensions whose choice was imposed by the user (the others were proposed by the AI).

commands.description: Shell commands of the project. Skills, hooks and CI run exactly these. Filled by the AI from the stack; extra keys allowed.

verify.description: The full quality gate: everything the contract requires, in one command.

workflow.description: How the work is carried out with the agent.

x-values.spec-driven: spec → plan → tasks → code; each step validated
x-values.tdd: spec-driven, and every behaviour starts with a failing test

plan_before_code.description: The agent presents a plan and waits for approval before writing code.

review.description: Review performed before a task is declared done.

x-values.self: the agent re-reads its own diff against the contract
x-values.agent: a dedicated reviewer sub-agent reviews the diff

agent_commits.description: The agent may run `git commit` / `git push`. When false, it proposes a commit message and the user commits.

hosting.x-effect: Selects the CI provider and enables PR templates and issues.

x-values.trunk: work directly on the main branch
x-values.feature-branches: one branch per task, merged through a pull request

issues.description: /plan creates issues on the hosting platform for each task.

formatter.description: An automatic formatter is configured and applied.

x-values.strict: recommended + stricter rules, warnings fail the gate

typecheck.description: Static typing strictness, when the language supports it.

max_complexity.description: Maximum cyclomatic complexity per function. 0 disables the check.

max_duplication_pct.description: Maximum share of duplicated code, in percent. 0 disables the check.

x-values.all: all code except generated code and configuration

integration.description: Scope of integration tests (database, external services, API).

coverage_min.description: Minimum line coverage, in percent, excluding generated code and configuration. 0 disables the check. /review also checks that tests make real assertions, so coverage is not gamed.

mutation.description: Mutation testing, to measure how much the tests actually catch.

level.description: Security level, mapped onto the levels of the reference standards in `standards` (e.g. OWASP ASVS L1–L3).

x-values.2: standard for apps handling sensitive data (ASVS L2)

standards.description: Reference security standards, chosen by the AI for the project's domain (e.g. OWASP ASVS, OWASP MASVS, ETSI EN 303 645).

x-values.report: vulnerabilities reported, the gate still passes
x-values.block: high or critical vulnerabilities fail the gate

threat_model.description: A threat model is written and maintained (docs/THREAT_MODEL.md).

personal.description: Whether the project handles personal data.

x-values.sensitive: special categories or high-impact data (e.g. health, finances, minors)

categories.description: Free list of notable data categories (e.g. health, financial, minors, location).

compliance.description: Regulatory frameworks that apply, chosen by the AI (e.g. GDPR, HDS).

migrations.description: Schema changes go through versioned migrations.

backups.description: Backups of persistent data are planned and restorable.

x-values.measured: targets defined and measured, not blocking
x-values.enforced: targets checked in CI; a regression fails the build

targets.description: Domain-specific targets proposed by the AI, as `<metric> = <number>` (e.g. `lcp_ms = 2500`, `api_p95_ms = 300`, `firmware_ram_kb = 256`).

load_testing.description: Load tests are written and run before releases.

x-values.basic: errors caught at the boundaries, clear message to the user
x-values.structured: typed errors, uniform error format for APIs

observability.description: What the running project reveals about itself.

error_tracking.description: Runtime errors are reported to an error tracker (Sentry-like).

metrics.description: Technical and business metrics are collected.

product_analytics.description: Product usage analytics (asked during the interview; off by default in every preset).

automated_checks.description: Automated accessibility checks run in the gate (e.g. axe).

locales.description: Locales of the user interface, the first one being the default.

ready.description: i18n infrastructure in place from the start, even with a single locale (no hard-coded user-facing strings).

docs.description: Framing and project documentation generated and maintained.

spec.description: docs/SPEC.md — problem, users, scope, non-goals (short for poc).

context_glossary.description: docs/CONTEXT.md — domain glossary used in code and conversation.

quality.description: docs/QUALITY.md — measurable requirements and how each is verified.

roadmap.description: docs/ROADMAP.md — produced by /plan (optional, offered during the interview).

toolchain.description: How tool versions are pinned and installed.

x-values.mise: mise.toml pins every tool; `mise install` sets up the machine

ci.description: Continuous integration runs `commands.verify` on every change. The provider follows `git.hosting`.

x-values.manual: deployment scripted, triggered by a human
x-values.auto: deployment triggered automatically after the gate passes

deploy_target.description: Free description of where the project is deployed (e.g. Vercel, Fly.io, VPS with Docker, app stores). Empty if not decided.

x-values.dev-services: local services (database, cache…) run in containers
x-values.full: the application itself is containerised too

devcontainer.description: A devcontainer describes the full development environment.

dependency_updates.description: Automated dependency update pull requests (Dependabot, Renovate…).

agent.description: Behaviour and configuration of AI agents on the project.

autonomy.description: How freely the agent acts; translated into each agent's permission settings.

x-values.supervised: asks before editing files or running commands
x-values.balanced: edits and runs project commands freely, asks for anything outside the project or irreversible
x-values.autonomous: acts freely within the project; still never commits unless allowed

adapters.description: Agents for which specific configuration is generated (e.g. claude, cursor, copilot). AGENTS.md is always generated.

mcp_servers.description: MCP servers configured for the project (e.g. context7, playwright).

hooks.description: Automatic actions run by agents that support hooks. For other agents, the same rules are written in AGENTS.md.

format_on_edit.description: Run the formatter after each file edit.

self_review.description: At the end of a turn that modified files, send the agent back once to re-read its diff against CONTEXT.md, the ADRs and QUALITY.md.

verify_on_stop.description: At the end of a turn, run `commands.verify`; on failure, send the agent back to fix it.

block_git_commit.description: Refuse `git commit` and `git push` from the agent. Defaults to the opposite of `workflow.agent_commits`.
